attachments.text:
ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2020-01-15
Provider: Dr. Aisha Patel, MD
Department: Neonatology
Visit Type: inpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Poor sleep and difficulty with feeding noted by nursing staff

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
This neonate presents for evaluation of poor sleep and feeding difficulties following earlier assessment for coughing and choking during feeds. He was born at term via uncomplicated vaginal delivery after limited prenatal care. Apgar scores were 8 and 9 at 1 and 5 minutes, respectively, with birth weight appropriate for gestational age; he did not require resuscitation. Over the past 48 hours, the nursing staff has noted episodes of high-pitched crying, tremors, and increased muscle tone. He is difficult to console and has frequent yawning and sneezing. During feeds, he becomes sweaty and irritable, with loose stools and occasional vomiting. His mother has a history of irregular prenatal visits and no medical conditions were documented during pregnancy.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Tracheoesophageal fistula with esophageal atresia (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Tracheoesophageal fistula with esophageal atresia (H-type)
- Neonatal abstinence syndrome

PAST SURGICAL HISTORY:
- Primary repair of tracheoesophageal fistula

MEDICATIONS:
Home Medications:
- Phenobarbital 2.5 mg/kg PO twice daily
- Omeprazole 0.7 mg/kg PO once daily

ALLERGIES:
No known drug allergies

FAMILY HISTORY:
There is no family history of congenital disorders

SOCIAL HISTORY:
No exposure to alcohol or tobacco was reported by the mother

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
Physical examination shows a thin, fussy neonate with tachycardia, dilated pupils, and excoriations on the face from persistent rubbing. There are no murmurs, dysmorphic features, or structural anomalies noted.

ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2020-03-15
Provider: Dr. David Chen, MD
Department: Emergency Medicine
Visit Type: ed

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Irritability and poor feeding for the past 24 hours with fever

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
The infant with history of tracheoesophageal fistula with esophageal atresia and neonatal abstinence syndrome returns for emergency evaluation. The mother reports that the infant has been less responsive and has a decreased appetite. She also noticed that his temperature has been fluctuating, with a recorded fever at home of 38.3°C (100.9°F) followed by periods of cool extremities.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Tracheoesophageal fistula with esophageal atresia (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Neonatal Abstinence Syndrome (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Tracheoesophageal fistula with esophageal atresia (H-type)

The infant was born at term via spontaneous vaginal delivery without complications. His prenatal course was unremarkable, and he was discharged from the hospital at 48 hours of life.

PAST SURGICAL HISTORY:
- Primary repair of tracheoesophageal fistula

MEDICATIONS:
Home Medications:
- Phenobarbital 2.5 mg/kg PO twice daily
- Omeprazole 0.7 mg/kg PO once daily

ALLERGIES:
No known drug allergies

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Maternal opioid use disorder
- Maternal tobacco and alcohol use denied during pregnancy
- No family history of congenital gastrointestinal anomalies

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: Never. Occupation: None (newborn).

VITAL SIGNS:
His temperature is 36.5°C (97.7°F), heart rate is 160 beats per minute, respiratory rate is 45 breaths per minute, and blood pressure is 65/40 mmHg.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On examination, the infant appears lethargic and has a weak cry. Capillary refill time is 3 seconds. The anterior fontanelle is full and tense. No rash is noted. Lung and heart examinations are unremarkable.

LABORATORY DATA:
Laboratory studies are obtained:

- White blood cell count: 18,000/mm³
- Hemoglobin: 14 g/dL
- Platelet count: 150,000/mm³
- C-reactive protein: 45 mg/L (normal <10 mg/L)
- Blood culture: Pending
- Urine culture: Pending
- Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) analysis: Pending

ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2020-01-15
Provider: Dr. Robert Kim, MD
Department: Pediatric Surgery
Visit Type: inpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Episodes of coughing and choking that occur during feeding

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
The mother reports that the infant turns blue and seems to struggle for air when attempting to breastfeed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Tracheoesophageal fistula with esophageal atresia (H-type)
- Neonatal abstinence syndrome

The pregnancy was unremarkable, and prenatal ultrasounds did not reveal any abnormalities.

PAST SURGICAL HISTORY:
- Primary repair of tracheoesophageal fistula

MEDICATIONS:
Home Medications:
- Phenobarbital 2.5 mg/kg PO twice daily
- Omeprazole 0.7 mg/kg PO once daily

ALLERGIES:
No known drug allergies

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Maternal opioid use disorder
- Maternal tobacco and alcohol use denied during pregnancy
- No family history of congenital gastrointestinal anomalies

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: Never. Occupation: None (newborn).

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On examination, the infant has a normal heart rate and respiratory rate, but mild intercostal retractions are noted. An attempt to pass a nasogastric tube meets resistance at approximately 10 cm from the nares

IMAGING:
A chest X-ray shows the coiled tube in the upper esophageal pouch
